data.gender_notes: Onesimus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek, Onesimus means "useful" or "profitable". This name was given to a runaway slave in the New Testament book of Philemon, who later returned to his master and was welcomed back. The name Onesimus carries the meaning “Useful, profitable” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Onesimus usually hope their child will grow to embody useful, profitable and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אונסימוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אונסימוס נגזר מהמילה היוונית ονόσμος (Onesimos), שפירושה 'מועיל' או 'מועילה'. באסטרולוגיה היוונית, השם אונסימוס היה מיועד לאלו שנולדו עם כוכבים טובים ומבשרים טובות. השם משמש גם בברית החדשה של התנך, בספר פילימון, כאחד מתלמידיו של פאולוס.

in_greek.name: Ὀνήσιμος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὀνήσιμος (Onesimos) σημαίνει 'χρήσιμος ἄνθρωπος' δηλαδή άνθρωπος χρήσιμος. Στο Καινή Διαθήκη, συγκεκριμένα στην Επιστολή προς Φιλήμονα, ο Ὀνήσιμος αναφέρεται ως ένας σκλάβος που δραπέτευσε και αργότερα έγινε Χριστιανός με τη βοήθεια του Παύλου.

in_latin.name: Onesimus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Onesimus is derived from the Greek word ονόσμος (Onesimos), meaning 'useful' or 'helpful'. In the early Christian Church, Onesimus was known as a slave who escaped and later became a Christian through the apostle Paul's influence. The name signifies someone who brings utility or benefit.

in_english.name: Onesimus
in_english.long_meaning: The name Onesimus originates from the Greek Ὀνήσιμος (Onesimos), meaning 'useful' or 'helpful'. It is prominently featured in the New Testament, specifically in the Epistle to Philemon, where Onesimus is a runaway slave who converts to Christianity through Paul's ministry. The name symbolizes someone who is beneficial or advantageous to others, reflecting virtues of utility and kindness.

data.cultural_impact: Onesimus, as a name, carries a rich historical significance as it was borne by a slave who made a significant transformation in the ancient world. The name Onesimus serves as a reminder of the transformative power of repentance, forgiveness, and redemption. In the New Testament, Onesimus was a runaway slave who was sent to Philemon, his master, by the Apostle Paul. Paul, writing on behalf of Onesimus, asked Philemon to forgive and welcome him back, demonstrating an incredible act of mercy and compassion. The story of Onesimus underscores the value and potential of every individual, regardless of their background or circumstances, which remains an important message in modern society.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Onesimus carries deep spiritual significance as it highlights the transformative power of God's love and forgiveness. Onesimus, a man once enslaved and considered worthless, was given a new identity and purpose by the Apostle Paul and God. Through Paul's intervention, Onesimus was restored to his rightful place as a brother and servant in Philemon's household. This story illustrates the biblical principle of redemption, as God sees us not as mere vessels of our past mistakes, but as valuable and precious children worthy of His love, forgiveness, and restoration. The name Onesimus serves as a reminder that no matter what our past may be, we can be transformed by God's grace and find new purpose in His service.
